title: Island of Ithaca Bets on Tourism After The Odyssey
paragraphs: Odysseus spent years trying to get back to Ithaca after the Trojan War. But for travelers today, going to Ithaca is as simple as getting on a ferry!
Ithaca is a small Greek island close to the larger island of Kefalonia. Like many other islands in the Ionian Sea, it's got beautiful blue waters and great weather most of the year.
But that's not the reason many travelers may soon be planning trips to Ithaca. Fans of The Odyssey may be hoping to see Odysseus' home island for themselves!

Based on the epic poem by Homer — believed to have been written around 2,700 years ago — Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey was released in cinemas in many parts of the world in July. The movie has been a huge success, making more than $1 billion around the world in less than a month.

Ithaca isn't as popular a destination as other Greek islands, but locals think the movie will change that. Mayor Dionysis Stanitsas has said that, while there has not been a noticeable increase in tourists yet, he's expecting more people to visit next year.
And one business owner on the island told Euronews that he's spoken with tourists who believe the island will become more popular with travelers.
For others, visiting has already been a dream come true.
"I learned Greek when I was a child and I studied The Odyssey. I love Odysseus. This is my dream," one recent visitor told Euronews.
The easiest way to get to Ithaca is to fly to Kefalonia Airport and get a ferry across to the island.

Interestingly, no part of The Odyssey was actually filmed in Ithaca. The location used for Ithaca in the movie is Favignana, just off Sicily — so that little Italian island may soon be getting more visitors too!
